To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The service dimensions most important to East African customers are those related to the physical environment, the quality of the service encounter, and the quality and range of products.

1) the most important service attributes for customers of East African banks are: (i) the ability to meet their financial needs; (ii) a good reputation; (iii) the ability to offer a wide range of financial services and (iv) good staff.

the key drivers of consumer satisfaction in retail banking in East Africa are: staff friendliness and helpfulness, branch cleanliness, branch security, staff competence, branch convenience, and staff courtesy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the application of appropriate methodologies for service quality and consumer research in emerging markets.
understanding the requirements of a particular group of consumers and how these differ from those of other regions.
identifying the service attributes that are important to customers in emerging markets and how these influence consumer satisfaction.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the service quality of the retail banking industry in Kenya and Uganda is generally poor, and that there is a significant gap between the perceived quality of service provided and the level of service expected by consumers.
this research has shown that there are differences in the service attributes and service quality perceptions of consumers in emerging economies compared to developed economies.
the service dimensions of retail banking are not universal and that the dimensions that are most important are likely to be different in each country.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
service quality in East African retail banks is generally perceived as poor, with a significant proportion of consumers being dissatisfied.
service quality is a multidimensional construct and the relative importance of the various dimensions is dependent on the context.
the service quality model of Parasuraman et al. (1994) is applicable to East African retail banks, although the relative importance of service dimensions varies considerably.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the retail banking sector in East Africa is still in its infancy, with a large potential for growth.
the service dimensions most valued in emerging markets are those that are more difficult to deliver and which are more likely to vary from branch to branch.
the service quality of retail banks in East Africa is generally perceived to be poor and that there is considerable scope for improving customer satisfaction.
